page: Google Cloud Platform f1-micro is an entry-level, shared-core virtual machine instance belonging to the f1 server family. It features 1 vCPU mapped to a shared physical core on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor, paired with 0.6 GB of system memory. This configuration does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The underlying CPU architecture supports instruction set extensions such as AVX, AVX512F, AES cryptography, and Intel Hyper-Threading.

Performance benchmarks place this instance type in the bottom 10% across all tested categories. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both yield a score of 384.79, reflecting the shared-core resource allocation. Memory performance is constrained, with a read-only small-block cached bandwidth of 80.8 GB/sec and a large-block write bandwidth of 0.2 GB/sec. Database and web serving capabilities are similarly limited, with Redis SET operations reaching 0.24 million operations per second and static web serving throughput measuring 0.22 GB/sec.

Due to its shared-core architecture and minimal memory footprint, the f1-micro is highly cost-efficient for lightweight, non-production tasks. It is designed for low-resource workloads where continuous high CPU utilization is not required. Appropriate use cases include basic development environments, small-scale testing, low-traffic static web serving, and simple cron jobs or automation scripts.
